author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Tree Pipit (Anthus trivialis), adult, as seen in Korea on autumn migration: upperparts warm buff-brown with clear dark streaks on the crown and mantle, rump unstreaked; face rather plain, with a weak buffy-white supercilium and no dark spot at the rear of the ear-coverts; two pale wing-bars; dark malar stripe; throat whitish; breast buff with bold black streaks; flanks buff with only fine thin streaks; belly white; outer tail feathers white. Bill fine, dark above with a pinkish base below; dark eye; legs pink.
art.pose: walking on short grass under trees with the tail gently pumping, side view
art.scene: short grass and fallen leaves beneath trees on a Korean offshore island during autumn migration; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Slim pipit, a little larger than a sparrow. Bill fine and straight, shorter than the head, slightly stouter than Olive-backed Pipit's. Legs pink, medium length, with a short, arched hind claw. Tail medium-long with white outer feathers, gently pumped while walking. Walks on short grass under trees and flies up into branches when flushed.
avoid: Do not paint greenish upperparts, a bold black-and-white supercilium or a white-and-black spot on the rear ear-coverts; those mark Olive-backed Pipit (Anthus hodgsoni).
Do not paint heavily streaked flanks or white braces on the back (Red-throated Pipit, Anthus cervinus).
